title: Runtime profile metrics map (profile pack v1) — tags, cardinality, aggregation notes
content:
Context
- This doc maps the metrics + tags we need in runtime to validate “hardware tuning profiles pack” behavior across H100 / L40S / (preview) B200.
- Primary uses:
  1) rollout safety (Hosted canary + Dedicated opt-in)
  2) perf-canary gating (default profile changes)
  3) benchmark-lab attribution (store results keyed by profile version)
  4) triage: answer “what profile was active, what did the scheduler do, did kernels fall back, did memory fragment?”

Non-goals
- Not defining full dashboards here (see Confluence dashboard spec). This is the metric inventory + label strategy.
- Not proposing per-customer or per-request high-cardinality logging. Prefer sampled traces for request-level granularity.

Owners / review
- Owner: Allison Grant (obs/dashboards)
- Runtime instrumentation: Julian Moore (scheduler), Omar El-Sayed (KV/memory), Yuki Sato (kernel selection logging)
- Metrics ingestion constraints: Caleb Johnson
- SRE gates/alerts: Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes

----------------------------------------
1) Global labeling conventions (MUST / SHOULD)

MUST labels (allowed on all new runtime histograms/counters):
- env: hosted|dedicated|private
- region: e.g., us-east-1, eu-west-1 (existing)
- sku: H100|L40S|B200 (see compatibility: can be derived from GPU metadata)
- profile_id: stable identifier of active profile (e.g., h100-sxm-prod-default)
- profile_version: semantic-ish pack version (e.g., 1.0.0)
- runtime_version: e.g., 1.22.0 (already present in many places)

SHOULD labels (use only where they materially help and stay low-cardinality):
- driver_branch: e.g., r550, r555 (not full driver string)
- cuda_major: 12.4 / 12.5 (major.minor only)
- model_family: llama|mistral|qwen|mixtral|other (bucketed)
- workload_bucket: short_ctx|med_ctx|long_ctx|mixed (bucketed; defined by scheduler)
- route: only for a limited allowlist of core routes; avoid arbitrary customer-defined route names

NOT ALLOWED labels on metrics (high cardinality / PII / cost):
- request_id, session_id, prompt hash, customer_id (use traces/logs with access controls)
- full model_id including fine-tune or tenant suffixes (must be bucketed)
- full GPU UUID, node hostname, pod UID (use logs + inventory)

Note: We still want “which customer is impacted” views, but do it via controlled joins in internal tooling, not via raw metric labels.

----------------------------------------
2) Metric namespaces + types

Proposed namespace prefix:
- runtime.* (core runtime stats)
- runtime.scheduler.*
- runtime.kernel.*
- runtime.kv_cache.*
- runtime.memory.*
- runtime.admission.*

Metric type guidelines
- Latency: histogram (ms)
- Counts: counter
- Gauges: only for instantaneous state (e.g., active sequences), avoid per-request gauges

----------------------------------------
3) Required metrics map (v1)

A) Request / stage timing (validates “expected behavior” per SKU)

1) runtime.request_latency_ms (histogram)
- definition: end-to-end service latency (from request admitted to response done); stream vs non-stream should be separated
- labels: env, region, sku, profile_id, profile_version, workload_bucket, model_family, request_type
- request_type values: chat|completion|embeddings|rerank (keep limited)
- notes: do NOT add route by default; allowlist for core internal routes only

2) runtime.stage_latency_ms (histogram)
- definition: per-stage latency buckets; include queueing explicitly
- labels: env, region, sku, profile_id, profile_version, workload_bucket, model_family, stage
- stage values (fixed set):
  - queue
  - prefill_compute
  - decode_compute
  - kv_cache_ops (compaction/eviction)
  - tokenization (if in-runtime)
  - postprocess
- note: stage label is low-cardinality and preferred to “separate metrics per stage”.

3) runtime.scheduler_queue_ms (histogram)
- definition: time waiting in scheduler before first compute
- labels: env, region, sku, profile_id, profile_version, workload_bucket
- why separate: queueing is the first signal of overload / bad batching heuristics.

B) Scheduler + batching behavior (explains throughput/latency tradeoffs)

4) runtime.scheduler.active_sequences (gauge)
- definition: number of sequences currently tracked in scheduler
- labels: env, region, sku, profile_id, profile_version, workload_bucket

5) runtime.scheduler.batch_size_tokens (histogram)
- definition: tokens per batch (prefill + decode tracked separately)
- labels: env, region, sku, profile_id, profile_version, phase
- phase values: prefill|decode

6) runtime.scheduler.preemptions_total (counter)
- definition: number of preemption events (e.g., pausing lower priority work)
- labels: env, region, sku, profile_id, profile_version, reason
- reason values: queue_pressure|latency_slo|oom_risk|other

7) runtime.scheduler.bucket_assignment_total (counter)
- definition: count of requests assigned to each workload_bucket
- labels: env, region, sku, profile_id, profile_version, workload_bucket
- note: helps validate bucket distribution drift after profile changes.

C) Kernel selection / fallback (detect “we’re not using the intended fast path”)

8) runtime.kernel.choice_total (counter)
- definition: kernel variant chosen for attention (and any other major kernels we gate)
- labels: env, region, sku, profile_id, profile_version, model_family, kernel, variant
- kernel values: attention|paged_attention|fused_mlp (start with attention only if we want to limit)
- variant values: v1|v2|v3|fallback
- cardinality note: model_family OK; do NOT label with exact model name.

9) runtime.kernel.fallback_total (counter)
- definition: explicit fallback events (not just “variant=fallback”), with reason
- labels: env, region, sku, profile_id, profile_version, kernel, reason
- reason values: unsupported_shape|driver_incompat|oom_guardrail|numerics_guardrail|unknown

10) runtime.kernel.fallback_rate (derived)
- definition: fallback_total / choice_total aggregated over 5–10m
- use: alerting (see alert section)

D) KV cache + memory stability (most common “profile got riskier” regression)

11) runtime.kv_cache.bytes_in_use (gauge)
- definition: KV cache allocated bytes in use
- labels: env, region, sku, profile_id, profile_version, pool
- pool values: gpu|host (if applicable)

12) runtime.kv_cache.hit_ratio (gauge)
- definition: prefix/KV cache hit ratio (if implemented in this runtime path)
- labels: env, region, sku, profile_id, profile_version, model_family
- note: must be computed carefully (windowed); otherwise interpret as noisy.

13) runtime.kv_cache.evictions_total (counter)
- labels: env, region, sku, profile_id, profile_version, reason
- reason values: capacity|ttl|fragmentation|manual

14) runtime.kv_cache.compactions_total (counter)
- labels: env, region, sku, profile_id, profile_version

15) runtime.kv_cache.compaction_time_ms (histogram)
- labels: env, region, sku, profile_id, profile_version

16) runtime.memory.fragmentation_estimate (gauge)
- definition: runtime’s estimate of allocator fragmentation (0..1 or percent)
- labels: env, region, sku, profile_id, profile_version
- note: this is imperfect; still useful for correlation during tail latency / OOM events.

17) runtime.memory.oom_events_total (counter)
- definition: OOMs thrown in runtime or CUDA OOM mapped into a stable counter
- labels: env, region, sku, profile_id, profile_version, phase
- phase values: model_load|prefill|decode|kv_cache|other

18) runtime.memory.alloc_retries_total (counter)
- definition: allocator retry/backoff path taken (early signal before OOM)
- labels: env, region, sku, profile_id, profile_version

E) Admission control + overload behavior (how we degrade)

19) runtime.admission.rejections_total (counter)
- labels: env, region, sku, profile_id, profile_version, reason
- reason values: queue_limit|memory_headroom|rate_limit|circuit_breaker|other

20) runtime.admission.queue_limit (gauge)
- definition: effective queue limit after profile + dynamic adjustments
- labels: env, region, sku, profile_id, profile_version

21) runtime.admission.headroom_bytes (gauge)
- definition: configured headroom target (bytes) used for safety
- labels: env, region, sku, profile_id, profile_version

----------------------------------------
4) “Nice-to-have” metrics (v1.1 / if we can afford)

- runtime.scheduler.decode_tokens_per_step (histogram)
  Why: helps detect decode underutilization on H100 vs L40S.

- runtime.kernel.compile_cache_hits_total (counter)
  Why: if kernel selection includes compilation / caching decisions; can explain cold-start jitter.

- runtime.memory.cuda_graph_enabled (gauge or info metric)
  Why: debugging differences across profiles, but keep it as an “info metric” per process/pod.

----------------------------------------
5) Metric label cardinality budget (practical limits)

Assumptions (based on current ingestion experience):
- Histograms with > ~200 active time series per region per day become expensive/noisy.
- Anything that cross-multiplies (model_family x workload_bucket x sku x profile_id x request_type x region) should be kept intentionally sparse.

Rules of thumb
- Only add model_family and workload_bucket to a metric if it is actively used for a decision (alert/rollout gate/benchmark attribution).
- For request latency metrics, prefer:
  - request_type (small)
  - workload_bucket (small)
  - model_family (small)
  - avoid route unless allowlisted

Implementation note
- If we need “per model” detail, do it via benchmark-lab (offline) and traces (sampled), not metrics.

----------------------------------------
6) Aggregation / rollup strategy

Metrics (Prom/OTel)
- Keep raw histograms at 10s or 30s scrape intervals.
- For long retention, create recording rules / rollups:
  - p50/p95/p99 for runtime.request_latency_ms and runtime.scheduler_queue_ms
  - sum(rate()) for counters (oom, fallbacks, rejections)
- Rollups should be keyed primarily by: sku + profile_id + profile_version + region + env
- Optional splits for analysis: workload_bucket, model_family (only for a couple of top-level panels)

Benchmarks (benchmark-lab)
- Benchmark artifacts must include:
  - profile_version
  - profile_id
  - sku
  - driver_branch / cuda_major
  - git_sha
- Store raw benchmark tables outside the metrics system; dashboards should pull summary stats.

Traces (sampling)
- Add profile_id/profile_version/sku as attributes on spans.
- Sampling: bias sampling upward on error conditions (OOM, kernel fallback, high queueing) to improve debuggability without exploding volume.

----------------------------------------
7) Alerting notes (high level; details in Confluence)

Kernel fallback
- Alert on sustained increases in runtime.kernel.fallback_total rate OR fallback ratio.
- Threshold guidance (rough; revisit after canary):
  - H100: fallback ratio > 1% for attention kernel over 10m is suspicious
  - L40S: fallback ratio > 2% may be acceptable depending on shapes; page only if coincident with p95 regression

Queueing
- Alert when runtime.scheduler_queue_ms p95 increases by > X% relative to baseline for the same sku+profile_version cohort.
- Must avoid paging on expected peak traffic; consider burn-rate style logic.

OOM
- Any non-zero OOM burst should page for Hosted default profile cohorts; for Dedicated, may ticket unless it causes sustained errors.

----------------------------------------
8) Open questions / TODOs

- Do we want profile_id AND profile_version on every metric, or can we omit profile_version where profile_id is already versioned? (Current assumption: keep both; profile_id is stable “name”, profile_version is pack version.)
- Decide on driver/cuda labeling: store as “info metric” per pod, then join in dashboards? vs label on runtime.kernel.fallback_total only.
- Confirm model_family bucketing list with Applied ML (Jonas/Claire/Arjun) so we don’t have drift.
- Confirm whether request_type exists consistently across all entry points (chat/completions/embeddings). If not, remove and rely on route allowlist.

----------------------------------------
9) Changelog
- 2026-01-23: initial draft from dashboard spec kickoff
- 2026-02-06: added explicit NOT ALLOWED label list + driver/cuda bucketing
- 2026-02-14: added admission control metrics + suggested fallback reasons
- 2026-02-20: aligned stage breakdown naming with scheduler instrumentation (queue vs compute separation)
